dct_description_sm: The Dehcho leaders and decision makers need a better understanding of why some lakes have high mercury levels in fish (above consumption guidelines) whereas other lakes have low mercury levels in fish (below consumption guidelines). Scientists and community members alike want to know why the mercury levels in some fish species and lakes have increased over the last ten or fifteen years whereas mercury levels in other fish species and lakes have remained stable. If it is possible to ascertain why mercury levels are rising in some species and lakes (slower growth, longer food chains, greater potential for methylation), the Deh Cho leadership would like to know if there are mitigation strategies, and/or follow-up studies that would help to ensure safe food fishes for their members.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Freshwater quality
Health sciences and contaminants -> Traditional food
dct_title_s: Understanding and predicting fish mercury levels in the Dehcho region using models of bio-magnification and bio-accumulation
